attrs.evidence: emission_conformance.mjs 9/9 over 9 fixtures. THE FIXTURE FAMILY WAS CORRECTED AT B6.1: what B6 called the I-4c witness is add(input x, input y) with {x:2,y:3}, and 2+3 == 3+2, so it is exactly the SYMMETRIC fixture INSTANTIATION_FALSIFIERS I-4c rejects as 'a test whose output cannot reveal the defect it is named for'. It is KEPT under an honest name -- 'two-port collapse' -- because what it actually proves is worth having: it closes to the SAME closed template as add(const 2, const 3), so two different source and instantiation histories become indistinguishable to emission. The ACTUAL I-4c, x + (x + y) with {x:2,y:3}, is added beside it: 7 under the correct binding and 8 under the swap, and a distinct closed template (ctmpl-efba3154...) already, so no fixture had to be invented to force distinctness. E-F1 now uses an unconstrained quotient-visible drift and covers 9/9; E-8 keeps the commutativity-dependent equivalence and covers the 6 add-bearing fixtures. AND THE PASS HEADLINE IS DERIVED FROM MEASURED FIELDS. B6's summary line stated that a semantics-preserving allocation change moves target_term_sem_id and is refused on all 8, and that an alpha-equivalent emitter differs in id on every fixture -- both FALSE, and both contradicted by the cases printed immediately above them in the same run. The cases had been corrected when the measurement arrived; the summary kept the pre-measurement theory, and the summary is what lands in RESULTS.txt. Every quantity the final line states is now a field written by the case that measured it.

attrs.statement: THE CANONICAL EMITTER DETERMINISTICALLY REALISES ITS DECLARED RELATION, over a FAMILY of fixtures rather than the one witness it had. closed_template_sem_id -(emission_sem_id)-> target_term_sem_id, and a conformance record is those three fields and no more: the relation's id is CONSTANT across every fixture, because a per-fixture emission id would identify invocations rather than the relation -- instantiation-identity@1's finding, one relation downstream. VERIFICATION IS BY RECONSTRUCTION AND NOT BY SELF-AGREEMENT: the verifier rebuilds the closed template from (program, inputs), re-emits through the canonical emitter, and canonicalises with an oracle IT WAS HANDED rather than one the emitter chose. An emitter that produced the artifact and certified its identity would verify a wrong emission against itself. EMISSION IS A FUNCTION OF THE CLOSED TEMPLATE AND NOT OF THE PROGRAM, which the family MEASURES rather than assumes: add(const 2, const 3) and add(input x, input y) closed with {x:2,y:3} are THE SAME CLOSED TEMPLATE and emit identically. Instantiation has already erased the difference between a literal and a port bound to that literal, and an emitter producing different bytes for those two would be reading something it is not entitled to see. The check is the implication in the direction that can be wrong -- equal domain implies equal codomain, different domain implies no collision -- rather than a blanket injectivity claim that would be false. THREE IDENTITIES FORM A LADDER, AND EMISSION PROVES THE MIDDLE ONE. exact emitted BYTES --quotient alpha-renaming and label SPELLING--> target_term_sem_id --execute, normalise, decode--> outcome_sem_id. Different bytes may share a target_term_sem_id; different target_term_sem_ids may share an outcome_sem_id; this battery demonstrates BOTH. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RECEIPT IS EXACT: EmissionReceipt carries no byte digest, so it does not and MUST NOT claim 'these exact bytes were produced'. It proves that the closed template maps, under this emission semantics, to this canonical target-term identity. If byte reproducibility ever needs proving it belongs beside executable_artifact_id as PROVENANCE, not inside a semantic relation whose own codomain deliberately erases the spelling. B6 framed this as a PAIR -- canonical determinism against semantic equivalence -- which is right at the top and hides that target_term_sem_id sits BETWEEN bytes and meaning rather than at either end. AND THE TWO ADVERSARIES ARE DIFFERENT ANIMALS, which B6 fused. CANONICAL DRIFT (E-F1): same closed template, same relation id, a changed claim about the target term, therefore REFUSE -- it needs NO semantic equivalence and therefore applies to every fixture. SEMANTIC EQUIVALENCE (E-8): different target_term_sem_id, SAME meaning -- it requires a real equivalence and is applicable only where the fragment supplies one. Fused, the canonical-drift falsifier would lose its adversary the moment a non-commutative operator arrived, for a reason having nothing to do with what it proves. CANONICAL DETERMINISM: a structural change to the emitter moves target_term_sem_id and the receipt carrying it is REFUSED. SEMANTIC EQUIVALENCE: that same alternate emitter's output decodes to the same outcome. The first says the relation is a function; the second says target_term_sem_id identifies THIS emitter's output rather than the term's meaning. Collapsing them yields either 'reordering is a semantic change' or 'emission may drift as long as the answer matches', and the second is how a compiler stops being reproducible quietly. AND THE MUTATION THAT EXHIBITS THE PAIR HAD TO BE MEASURED. An ALPHA-EQUIVALENT alternate emitter produces the IDENTICAL target_term_sem_id on every fixture -- the canonical signature is byte-equivariant under alpha-renaming and label permutation by asserted law (L-BYTES-1) -- so renaming cannot witness this at all and the adversary must be STRUCTURAL. Reordering add's operands is meaning-preserving on THIS fragment because addition commutes, and would not be for a non-commutative operator; the caveat is part of the law rather than a footnote to it. NO NATIVE FILM IS REQUIRED OR USED. The transition relation carries its own evidence, and defining the emitter's correctness by what its output computes would put the runtime inside the compiler's contract -- the layer collapse lowering_spike.layer_separation exists to refuse. A downstream composition runs last and is LABELLED an integration theorem; every conformance case stands without it.
